School: ^The new school didn’t have many trees yet, so the courtyard was always bathed in sunlight—especially in the afternoon. There were three buildings, but only one contained classrooms; since it was only two stories high, the different grade levels had to split the day, attending in either the morning or afternoon shifts. I recognized this place—I had definitely studied here before. I followed Ann into the classroom—the first one in the row on the first floor. Ann and I sat side-by-side at the fourth desk in the second row from the door. To my surprise, I was able to find my seat without having to ask anyone; perhaps this is what they call "muscle memory."
^Not long after we arrived, the bell rang for class to begin. The boy sitting in front of us turned around.
^"Hello. Did you study?" he asked, looking quite relaxed. I knew him. He was…
^"Morning, Kento. I studied a bit. Mokusa didn’t even remember there was a test today!"
^"Eh? Are you going to be okay?" His expression mirrored Ann’s—a mix of surprise and concern.
^"I’ll be fine. I’m not too worried about English."
^"Yeah, that’s true—English probably won’t give you any trouble."
^I nodded. I was quite confident in my English; a standard classroom test wouldn’t be an issue at all.

^He really was Kento—I had definitely been in class with him before. And the other students looked incredibly familiar, too. Perhaps my memories weren’t entirely gone; maybe they could still be recovered.

c-0: ^The bell rang, signaling the end of the homeroom period. It was almost time for the test. Once the papers had been handed out and the teacher had finished explaining the exam, the bell rang once more—this time, marking the start of the test.

AfterExam1: ^As the test concluded and all papers were submitted, the class said goodbye to the teacher, and everyone began comparing their answers.
^One soldier down. As for me, I started checking my answers with Kento and Ann.
